DEPARTMENT 730 LAW AND MOTION RULINGS


Case Number: 24STCV19779    Hearing Date: July 1, 2026    Dept: 730

Superior Court of California 

County of Los Angeles 

Department 730 

¿ 

VAROOJ ARAKELIAN, 

Plaintiff, 

vs. 

CITY OF LOS ANGELES; LOS ANGELES UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT (“LAUSD”); NEUTRON HOLDINGS, INC. dba LIME; and DOES 1 to 50, inclusive, 

Defendants. 

Case No.: 

24STCV19779 

Hearing Date: 

July 1, 2026 

 

 

[TENTATIVE] ORDER RE: MOTION TO BE RELIEVED AS COUNSEL 

 

I. BACKGROUND 

Plaintiff Varooj Arakelian (“Arakelian”) was riding Defendant Neutron Holdings, Inc.’s (“Lime”) scooter in front of Defendant Los Angeles Unified School District’s (“LAUSD”) premises when he ran over an uplifted sidewalk crack, causing him to fall off the scooter. Arakelian sues Defendants for products liability and premises liability. 

On April 30, 2026, Arakelian’s attorney, Robert L. Booker II (“Booker”), filed this instant motion to be relieved as counsel for Arakelian.  

No opposition has been filed to date. 

 

II. LEGAL STANDARD 

The process to be relieved as counsel of record requires: (1) “[a] notice of motion and motion to be relieved as counsel under Code of Civil Procedure section 284(2) must be directed to the client and must be made on the Notice of Motion and Motion to be Relieved as Counsel— Civil (form MC-051)” (Cal. Rules of Court, rule 3.1362, subd. (a))[1]1; (2) a declaration on the Declaration in Support of Attorney's Motion to Be Relieved as Counsel-Civil (form MC-052), which “must state in general terms and without compromising the confidentiality of the attorney client relationship why a motion under Code of Civil Procedure section 284(2) is brought instead of filing a consent under Code of Civil Procedure section 284(1) (rule 3.1362, subd. (c)); (3) a proposed order relieving counsel must be prepared on the Order Granting Attorney’s Motion to Be Relieved as Counsel—Civil (form MC-053),” “must be lodged with the court with the moving papers,” and “must specify all hearing dates scheduled in the action or proceeding, including the date of trial, if known” (rule 3.1362, subd. (e)); and (4) “[t]he notice of motion and motion, declaration, and the proposed order must be served on the client and on all other parties who have appeared in the case” along with additional requirements depending on the type of service (rule 3.1362, subd. (d)). 

The Court has discretion to allow an attorney to withdraw, and such a motion should be granted if there is no prejudice to the client and it does not disrupt the orderly process of justice. (Ramirez v. Sturdevant (1994) 21 Cal.App.4th 904, 915.) “After the order is signed, a copy of the signed order must be served on the client and on all parties that have appeared in the case. The court may delay the effective date of the order relieving counsel until proof of service of a copy of the signed order on the client has been filed with the court.” (Rule 3.1362, subd. (e).) 

 

III. DISCUSSION 

Here, Booker submitted completed MC-051, MC-052 and MC-053 forms in compliance with the rule 3.1362 requirements. Booker submitted a declaration stating that there have been irreconcilable breakdowns in the attorney-client relationship and attorney-client communication. (MC-052 ¶ 2(a)(2).) Booker asserts he served Arakelian at his last known address via mail, with return receipt requested. (MC-052 ¶ 3(b)(1)(a).) Booker also attempted to confirm Arakelian’s address by calling Arakelian’s telephone number. (MC-052 ¶ 3(b)(2)(a-b).) 

The Court previously heard this motion on June 4, 2026. In its minute order, the Court noted that Booker did not comply with the service requirements. Rule 3.1362, subdivision (d), requires the notice of motion, motion, declaration, and proposed order be “served on the client and on all other parties who have appeared in this case.” Booker has submitted proof of service on Defendants for the notice of motion, motion and declaration, but no proof of service for the proposed order. Additionally, Booker failed to submit proof of service for Arakelian for any of the filed papers. The Court noted that attestation of service under MC-052 ¶ 3 does not satisfy the proof of service requirements. The Court then continued the hearing to allow Booker to comply with the service requirements and ordered that he provide proof of service at least 5 days prior to the continued hearing date.  

As of June 30, 2026, the only new filing Booker provided with the Court following the Court’s June 4, 2026 minute order is proof of service on Defendants and Arakelian for the proposed order. Therefore, Booker is still not in compliance with the service requirements and has shown no efforts to submit proof of service for Arakelian of the notice of motion, motion, and declaration.  

Therefore, the Court DENIES the motion to be relieved as counsel. 

 

IV. CONCLUSION 

The Court DENIES the motion to be relieved as counsel. 

 

Moving Party is ordered to give notice. 

 

DATED: July 1, 2026 

__________________________ 

Hon. Alexander C.D. Giza 

Judge of the Superior Court

Case Number: 25STCV19253    Hearing Date: July 1, 2026    Dept: 730

Superior Court of California 

County of Los Angeles 

Department 730 

¿ 

YKILI ROSS, Cestni Que Vie Trust (CQV) established under Public Presumption - Private Living Man rebuts all presumption of wardship, infant estate, or U.S. citizenship Corpus Juris Secundum (CJS) - All Rights Reserved. Ykili: of Ross Township as Executor ) of Office, and Sole Heir of Estate Debtor Entity exists solely In commercial fiction) - controlled by private creditor U.S. Citizen status rebutted - Living Man holds no allegiance to foreign corporate jurisdictions, 

Plaintiff, 

vs. 

USC CREDIT UNION, 

Defendant. 

Case No.: 

25STCV19253 

Hearing Date: 

July 1, 2026 

 

 

[TENTATIVE] ORDER RE: MOTION TO QUASH SERVICE 

 

I. BACKGROUND 

Plaintiff Ykili Ross (“Plaintiff”), in pro per, filed this action against Defendant USC Credit Union (“Defendant”) on July 2, 2025. This action arises from Defendant’s alleged retention of estate instruments, failure to provide lawful accounting, misrepresentation of financial obligations, and interference with Plaintiff’s rights.  

On July 21, 2025, Plaintiff filed proof of service on Defendant by mail and acknowledgment of receipt of service on July 7, 2025, to an address outside California with return receipt requested.  

On September 11, 2025, Plaintiff again filed proof of service on Defendant by mail and acknowledgement of receipt of service but neglected to fill out information regarding how and where service took place.  

On February 9, 2026, Plaintiff filed a first amended complaint, with causes of action for (1) quiet title, (2) declaratory relief, and (3) breach of fiduciary duty.  

On April 9, 2026, Plaintiff filed a motion for leave to file a second amended complaint. 

On April 10, 2026, Defendant filed the instant motion to quash service of summons. 

On April 15, 2025, Plaintiff filed a declaration with the Court in opposition to the instant motion. 

On April 16, 2026, the Court denied Plaintiff’s motion for leave to file a second amended complaint. 

On May 4, 2025, Defendant filed a notice of non-receipt of Plaintiff’s opposition to the instant motion. 

On May 5, 2026, Plaintiff filed his opposition. 

As of June 26, 2026, Defendant has not filed a reply.  

 

II. LEGAL STANDARD 

“[C]ompliance¿with the statutory procedures for service of process is essential to establish personal¿jurisdiction. [Citation.]” (Dill v. Berquist Construction Co.¿(1994) 24 Cal.App.4th 1426, 1444.)¿¿¿ 

When a defendant challenges the court’s personal¿jurisdiction¿on the ground of improper service of process, the burden is on the plaintiff to prove the existence of¿jurisdiction¿by proving the facts requisite to an effective service. (Summers v. McClanahan¿(2006) 140 Cal.App.4th 403, 413.) “The filing of a proof of service creates a rebuttable presumption that the service was proper. However, the presumption arises only if the proof of service¿complies with¿the applicable statutory requirements.” (Floveyor¿Internat., Ltd. v. Superior Court¿(1997) 59 Cal.App.4th 789, 790.)¿¿ 

“ ‘On a motion to quash service of summons, the plaintiff bears the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that all jurisdictional criteria are met. [Citations.] The burden¿must be met by competent evidence in¿affidavits¿and authenticated documents; an unverified complaint may not be considered as supplying the necessary facts.’ [Citation.]” (Brown v. Garcia¿(2017) 17 Cal.App.5th 1198, 1203; see also¿Sheard v. Superior Court¿(1974) 40 Cal.App.3d 207, 211 [“[W]here a defendant properly moves to quash service of summons the burden is on the plaintiff to prove facts requisite to the effective service.”].)¿ 

 

III. DISCUSSION 

Defendant moves for an order quashing service of summons and the complaint against Plaintiff. Defendant contends service was improperly made on Defendant’s counsel, who is not authorized to accept service of process on Defendant’s behalf. (Mallari Decl., ¶ 2.)  

The Court agrees that the proofs of service are inadequate. The burden to show proper service is on Plaintiff. (Brown, supra,¿ 17 Cal.App.5th at p. 1203.) However, Plaintiff fails to show proper service on Defendant. 

“A summons may be served on a corporation by delivering a copy of the summons and the complaint by any of the following methods: (a)¿To the person designated as agent for service of process …; (b)¿To the president, chief executive officer, or other head of the corporation, a vice president, a secretary or assistant secretary, a treasurer or assistant treasurer, a controller or chief financial officer, a general manager, or a person authorized by the corporation to receive service of process; (c)¿If the corporation is a bank, to a cashier or assistant cashier or to a person specified in subdivision (a) or (b); …” (Code Civ. Proc., § 416.10.) 

Defendant’s counsel, Lorie Mallari (“Mallari”), received a package at her offices from Plaintiff mailed via U.S. Postal Service on March 6, 2026. (Mallari Decl., ¶ 2.) The package included the following documents: Form POS-040 Proof of Service by Mail; Form CIV-100 Request for Entry of Judgment and Court Judgment; Form JUD-100 of a Judgment; Sworn Declaration and Notice of Non Compliance in support of Request for Default, Demand for Accounting, and Immediate Adjudication, Transfer of Consideration, and Corrective Tax Reporting; Request for Judicial Notice; and a Declaration of True Ownership, First Creditor Status, and Right to Full Accounting and Transparency. (Mallari Decl., ¶ 2; Exh. A.) Mallari is not the registered agent of process with the California Secretary of State and is not authorized to accept service. (Mallari Decl., ¶¶ 3-4.) Rather, Douglas Kasper is the agent for service of process for Defendant. (Mallari Decl., ¶ 3.) 

In October 2025, Defendant learned of Plaintiff’s action against it. (Mallari Decl., ¶ 5.) On October 30, 2025 and February 23, 2026, the Court held order to show cause hearings regarding Plaintiff’s service on Defendant, which Plaintiff failed to attend. (Mallari Decl., ¶ 6.) As of the filing of this motion, Plaintiff has not properly served Defendant’s registered agent. (Mallari Decl., ¶ 7.) 

Therefore, Plaintiff failed to comply with Code of Civil Procedure section 416.10 for service on corporations, as Mallari does not qualify as a person who may be served on Defendant’s behalf under the statute. 

In opposition, Plaintiff appears to be confused about the issues set for hearing with this motion. Plaintiff’s opposition claims to “specially appear,” requests that the Court order Defendant to produce documents for discovery and compel the deposition of a competent representative. (Opp., 3:3-8.) These issues do not pertain to the motion to quash, so the Court will not address them. The only argument Plaintiff provides pertaining to the instant motion is that “Defendant’s motion to quash improperly attempts to avoid adjudication on the merits by raising procedural objections that are contradicted by evidence of service and actual notice. Plaintiff has demonstrated proper mailing, notice, and Defendant’s participation through counsel.” (Opp., 1:20-22.) However, as discussed above, Plaintiff has not demonstrated proper mailing and notice. (Code Civ. Proc., § 416.10.) Likewise, Plaintiff did not meet his burden of showing proper service. 

Therefore, the Court GRANTS Defendant’s motion to quash. 

 

IV. CONCLUSION 

The Court GRANTS Defendant’s motion to quash service. 

 

Moving Party is ordered to give notice. 

 

DATED: July 1, 2026 

__________________________ 

Hon. Alexander C.D. Giza 

Judge of the Superior Court

Case Number: 25STCV28783    Hearing Date: July 1, 2026    Dept: 730

Superior Court of California 

County of Los Angeles 

Department 730 

¿ 

BELLA ASSETS, LLC, 

Plaintiff, 

vs. 

VASANTA LLC, PREMIER AGENT NETWORK, INC., DIMITRI CHAMI, and DOES 1 through 50, inclusive, 

Defendants. 

Case No.: 

25STCV28783 

Hearing Date: 

July 1, 2026 

 

 

[TENTATIVE] ORDER RE: MOTION TO BE RELIEVED AS COUNSEL 

 

I. BACKGROUND 

Plaintiff Bella Assets, LLC (“Bella Assets”) purchased residential real property in Los Angeles inside a designated local historic district subject to significant restrictions. Defendants Vasanta LLC, Premier Agent Network, Inc., and Dimitri Chami did not disclose these restrictions and designation to Bella Assets during the sale of the property.  

On February 5, 2026, Bella Assets filed a substitution of attorney with the Court, which was stricken by the Court on May 21, 2026. The Court ordered Jin to file a motion to be relieved as counsel. 

On May 21, 2026, Bella Assets’ counsel, Jewels J. Jin/Jewels Jin Esquire APC (“Jin”), filed this instant motion to be relieved as counsel for Bella Assets. 

No opposition has been filed to date.   

 

II. LEGAL STANDARD 

The process to be relieved as counsel of record requires: (1) “[a] notice of motion and motion to be relieved as counsel under Code of Civil Procedure section 284(2) must be directed to the client and must be made on the Notice of Motion and Motion to be Relieved as Counsel— Civil (form MC-051)” (Cal. Rules of Court, rule 3.1362, subd. (a))[1]1; (2) a declaration on the Declaration in Support of Attorney's Motion to Be Relieved as Counsel-Civil (form MC-052), which “must state in general terms and without compromising the confidentiality of the attorney client relationship why a motion under Code of Civil Procedure section 284(2) is brought instead of filing a consent under Code of Civil Procedure section 284(1) (rule 3.1362, subd. (c)); (3) a proposed order relieving counsel must be prepared on the Order Granting Attorney’s Motion to Be Relieved as Counsel—Civil (form MC-053),” “must be lodged with the court with the moving papers,” and “must specify all hearing dates scheduled in the action or proceeding, including the date of trial, if known” (rule 3.1362, subd. (e)); and (4) “[t]he notice of motion and motion, declaration, and the proposed order must be served on the client and on all other parties who have appeared in the case” along with additional requirements depending on the type of service (rule 3.1362, subd. (d)). 

The Court has discretion to allow an attorney to withdraw, and such a motion should be granted if there is no prejudice to the client and it does not disrupt the orderly process of justice. (Ramirez v. Sturdevant (1994) 21 Cal.App.4th 904, 915.) “After the order is signed, a copy of the signed order must be served on the client and on all parties that have appeared in the case. The court may delay the effective date of the order relieving counsel until proof of service of a copy of the signed order on the client has been filed with the court.” (Rule 3.1362, subd. (e).) 

 

III. DISCUSSION 

Here, Jin submitted completed MC-051, MC-052, and MC-053 forms in compliance with the rule 3.1362 requirements. Jin originally failed to submit the MC-052 form and instead filed a separate declaration as an attachment to the MC-051 form stating there have been irreconcilable differences and circumstances arising between Jin and Bella Assets such that continued representation has become untenable. (Jin Decl., ¶ 2.) However, the following day after submitting the MC-051 and MC-053 forms, Jin submitted an MC-052 form. Jin asserts she served Bella Assets at their last known address via mail, with return receipt requested. (MC-052 ¶ 3(b)(1)(a).)  

On May 22, 2026, Jin filed a proof of service showing service of the declaration on Defendants. On June 2, 2026, Jin filed proof of service with the Court demonstrating service of the MC-051, MC-052, and MC-053 forms on Bella Assets, but the proof of service does not show service on Defendants. (POS-030.) Therefore, Jin did not comply with the service requirements under Rule 3.1362, subdivision (d), which requires the notice of motion, motion, declaration, and proposed order be “served on the client and on all other parties who have appeared in this case.” 

Therefore, the Court DENIES the motion to be relieved as counsel. 

 

IV. CONCLUSION 

The Court DENIES the motion to be relieved as counsel. 

Moving Party is ordered to give notice. 

 

DATED: July 1, 2026 

__________________________ 

Hon. Alexander C.D. Giza 

Judge of the Superior Court
